high-impact-actions.name: Wynes and Nicholas review of high-impact personal climate actions
high-impact-actions.outcome: Car-free living saves about 2.4 t CO2e a year; each round-trip transatlantic flight avoided 1.6 t; plant-based diet about 0.8 t, roughly 4 times recycling
high-impact-actions.limits: Averages from 39 studies, mostly in rich countries; one person's savings depend on their grid, car and diet. Green energy purchases were 'sometimes but not always' high impact.
high-impact-actions.locator: "living car-free for a year saves 2.4 tonnes"

food-footprints.name: Poore and Nemecek food emissions meta-analysis (via Our World in Data)
food-footprints.outcome: 1 kg of beef emits about 60 kg CO2e versus about 1 kg for peas; transport is under 10% of most foods' emissions
food-footprints.limits: Global averages; individual farms vary widely. Summary article, not the paper itself, was opened.
food-footprints.locator: "it is not the location that makes the carbon footprint of your dinner large"

home-energy-uses.name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) Residential Energy Consumption Survey: how homes use energy
home-energy-uses.outcome: Space heating and air conditioning are 52% of household energy use; water heating, lighting and refrigeration 25%
home-energy-uses.limits: National average from 2020; share varies a lot by climate and home size. Heating and cooling are not split out.
home-energy-uses.locator: "space heating and air conditioning" account for 52%

epa-footprint-calculator.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) household carbon footprint calculator
epa-footprint-calculator.outcome: Free calculator covering home energy, vehicles and waste; gives estimated pounds of CO2 a year against the US average and shows savings from planned actions
epa-footprint-calculator.limits: Leaves out food and flights, which can be large parts of a footprint.

denver-ebike-rebates.name: Denver e-bike rebate program
denver-ebike-rebates.outcome: The $4.7 million program launched in spring 2022; 67% of funds went to income-qualified residents with $1,200 vouchers (others got $400); riders averaged 26 miles a week and replaced 3.4 round-trip car trips; 71% drove less
denver-ebike-rebates.limits: Self-reported survey from the first nine months; mileage figures differ in later city statements. Rebate rounds sold out quickly.
denver-ebike-rebates.locator: "67% of the program's funds went to income-qualified residents"

utah-plug-in-solar.name: Utah plug-in solar law (HB 340)
utah-plug-in-solar.outcome: Utah became the first state to allow residents to plug solar systems directly into home outlets; passed with no dissenting votes; output up to 1,200 watts; inverters about $300 and panels $250 to $1,000 versus a $30,000 rooftop quote; in Germany balcony panels added 10% more solar capacity
utah-plug-in-solar.limits: A 1,200-watt system covers only part of a household's use. Grist reported that no complete plug-in system had been certified by UL yet; individual components were certified.
utah-plug-in-solar.locator: "No plug-in systems have been certified by UL to date"

federal-credit-ended.name: IRS energy efficient home improvement credit (25C)
federal-credit-ended.outcome: 30% credit, up to $2,000 a year for heat pumps, applied only to property placed in service before December 31, 2025
federal-credit-ended.limits: The credit has ended for new installations; only 2025 work can still be claimed.
federal-credit-ended.locator: "on or after Jan. 1, 2023, and before December 31, 2025"

home-energy-rebates.name: State home energy rebate programs (HEAR / HEEHRA)
home-energy-rebates.outcome: Point-of-sale rebates up to $8,000 for a heat pump for income-qualified households where states have launched
home-energy-rebates.limits: Seen only in search summaries from vendor blogs; many states have not launched, some returned funds, and California's were fully reserved by February 2026.

minnesota-community-solar.name: Minnesota community solar garden program
minnesota-community-solar.outcome: 939 MW in 2024, almost a third of the state's solar; subscribers' bills expected to fall 3% to 8%; repeal dropped in June 2025 after advocates rallied
minnesota-community-solar.limits: Non-subscribers who aren't low or moderate income may see bills rise 2% to 3%; Xcel Energy supported ending the program. Rules differ by state.
minnesota-community-solar.locator: Article dated June 23, 2025; bills lower by 3% to 8%

solar-united-neighbors-coops.name: Solar United Neighbors solar co-ops
solar-united-neighbors-coops.outcome: Co-ops organized by Solar United Neighbors are member-driven groups of about 100 neighbors; bulk purchasing brings discounted pricing; each member signs their own individual contract
solar-united-neighbors-coops.limits: The co-ops page gives no savings figures, and doesn't say how the installer is chosen or whether joining is free. Pricing claims come from the organizer.

middelgrunden-coop.name: Middelgrunden wind turbine cooperative
middelgrunden-coop.outcome: 8,553 members own 10 of the 20 offshore turbines; the farm supplies about 4% of Copenhagen's electricity
middelgrunden-coop.limits: Built with Danish rules that favored local ownership; the other half belongs to the city utility.

mce-community-choice.name: MCE (Marin Clean Energy) community choice program
mce-community-choice.outcome: Cities and county pooled residents' buying power; customers could choose 27% renewable Light Green or 100% renewable Deep Green
mce-community-choice.limits: Only some states allow community choice programs; the profile page is from an advocacy site and gives no recent customer figures.
mce-community-choice.locator: Deep Green described as "100% renewable energy"

held-v-montana.name: Held v. Montana
held-v-montana.outcome: Montana Supreme Court, December 18, 2024, upheld 16 young plaintiffs: the state's environmental right includes a stable climate; two 2023 laws limiting climate review struck down
held-v-montana.limits: Applies only under Montana's constitution; the state argued climate policy belongs to lawmakers, and people disagree about courts' role.

climate-cafes.name: Climate cafes
climate-cafes.place: Began in rural Scotland; now in Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal and elsewhere
climate-cafes.outcome: Informal groups to talk through climate feelings, inspired in part by death cafes; a Canadian study in Social Science & Medicine interviewed 17 people and found them safe, judgment-free spaces
climate-cafes.limits: Research is sparse and small; cafes vary, and many deliberately don't focus on action.
climate-cafes.locator: Study described as "the first of its kind in Canada"

yale-opinion-maps.name: Yale Climate Opinion Maps
yale-opinion-maps.outcome: 72% of Americans think global warming is happening; estimates down to state, county and congressional district
yale-opinion-maps.limits: Modeled estimates from national surveys, not a count of every person.
yale-opinion-maps.locator: "72% of Americans think global warming is happening"

google-flights-emissions.name: Google Flights emissions estimates
google-flights-emissions.outcome: Each flight labeled higher, typical or lower emissions against the route median; nonstop is not always lowest
google-flights-emissions.limits: Estimates from a model or the European aviation safety agency's label; some flights are marked unknown.
google-flights-emissions.locator: Help article: labels higher, typical, lower, or unknown emissions

rewiring-america-api.name: Rewiring America incentives API
rewiring-america-api.outcome: Free API with electrification incentive programs and eligibility, plus an address-based model of upgrade effects
rewiring-america-api.limits: Coverage depends on the group keeping programs current; rebates change quickly.

epa-power-profiler.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Power Profiler (eGRID)
epa-power-profiler.outcome: Enter a ZIP code and utility to see your grid region's fuel mix and emissions against the national average
epa-power-profiler.limits: The page opened but the tool itself did not render in my fetch; how it works comes from older articles. Data year 2023.

fema-risk-index.name: FEMA National Risk Index in the Resilience Analysis and Planning Tool
fema-risk-index.outcome: Risk data for 18 natural hazards in a public mapping tool
fema-risk-index.limits: The old risk index site now redirects here; I couldn't confirm street-level detail or which hazards are mapped by tract.
fema-risk-index.locator: NRI v1.20 update on RAPT, 18 natural hazards

open-states.name: Open States (now Plural) legislative data
open-states.outcome: Data on state legislators and bills, with APIs, bulk downloads and a free legislator lookup
open-states.limits: Now run by a company (Plural / SAI360); API terms could change.
